zone-governance.title: Implement a zoned governance strategy – Microsoft Copilot Studio
zone-governance.notes: Zoned governance means splitting environments into segments and applying different governance policies depending on the purpose and risk level of an agent. The goal is to steer agent creation according to risk and technical complexity. Agents live in Power Platform environments, and those environments determine data location, permissions, connector allowance and the separation of development, test and production. The guidance describes three zones: citizen development for personal and team agents, partnered development for IT-approved makers building for other teams, and professional development for pro developers building business-critical agents. Zone one is limited to Microsoft 365 and Power Platform connectors and keeps sharing off, while the later zones add scoped roles, IT approval before publishing, ALM pipelines and the strictest security controls. Controls can be applied at tenant, environment, agent and maker-access level, for example through data policies, network isolation, authentication settings and security groups. Monitoring runs through the Power Platform admin center, the Microsoft admin center and Microsoft Purview. The page does not name licensing requirements for the zone model itself and does not list explicit limitations.

swimlane-diagram.title: Create a cross-functional flowchart – Microsoft Support (Visio)
swimlane-diagram.notes: A cross-functional flowchart, often called a swimlane diagram, shows how a business process relates to the functional units that carry it out. Each swimlane stands for a unit such as a department or a position, and every process step is placed in the lane of the party responsible for it. Lanes can run horizontally or vertically, and the orientation can be chosen at creation and changed later. Separator lines mark phase changes such as the move from one milestone to the next, and containers can outline groups of related shapes. Lanes can be added through the header context menu, a ribbon command, dragging from the stencil or a corner arrow, and lane labels can be rotated. Shapes move with a lane only when the lane contains them, and deleting a lane also deletes the shapes inside it. In Visio, the diagram is built from the Cross-Functional Flowchart template in the Flowchart category, or generated from Excel data with a Data Visualizer diagram. The page covers Visio Plan 1 and Visio Professional or Standard 2016, 2021 and 2024, and notes that the web version needs Visio Plan 1.
